help.title: Help: prediction parameters
help.intro:
Values on the Settings tab are saved automatically and applied to checked WAV files when you click Start predictions.

Typical workflow:
1. Set model, threshold, and paths in the parameters block.
2. Check WAV files in the table (add files in Projects).
3. Run predictions — orcAI writes a label text file for each recording.
4. On Analysis, review the spectrogram and filter labels by duration if needed.

Signal classes are defined in the selected model’s orcai_parameter.json—you tune sensitivity and output paths here, not class names.

filterNote.title: How this relates to filtering
filterNote.body: Filtering on the Filter tab is a separate step after predictions: it reads an existing label file and removes segments whose duration does not match project rules (*_call_duration_limits.json). The label suffix in the filter must match the Label suffix in the model parameters Additional section.

model.title: Model
model.what: The neural network that detects sound events in a recording. Each model ships with orcai_parameter.json: class list (signal types), spectrogram settings, and network layout. Built-in orcai-isl-v1 suits typical field audio; trained checkpoints appear from the project folder.
model.effect: The model defines which classes can be detected and how output files are named—the model id is part of the filename. Different models on the same WAV produce different result files you can compare on the spectrogram.
model.example:
Recording: night_01.wav
Model: orcai-isl-v1
Output (with path default):
night_01_c1_orcai-isl-v1_predicted.txt
model.tip: Run a small package first with orcai-isl-v1. For custom training, pick the checkpoint you trained. See class names in the model’s orcai_parameter.json or in the spectrogram legend after a run.

channel.title: Channel
channel.what: Which channel in a multichannel WAV orcAI analyzes. Numbering starts at 1 (first channel = 1, second = 2, …). For standard mono files, always use 1.
channel.effect: The spectrogram and detector use only this channel. Label filenames include _c1_, _c2_, etc. The wrong channel can yield empty or noisy results even when the target signal is clear on another channel.
channel.example:
File stereo_trap.wav (2 channels):
channel 1 — trap mic with calls → use 1
channel 2 — background noise → not for target predictions
channel.tip: Match the channel used during model training. If unsure, listen in Audacity and pick the channel where the signal is clearest.

threshold.title: Confidence threshold
threshold.what: Minimum model confidence from 0.00 to 1.00. A time region is written to the label file only if the model is confident enough that one of the classes from orcai_parameter.json is present.
threshold.effect: Low (0.30–0.45): more labels, including weak and possible false positives. Mid (0.50): balanced starting point. High (0.65–0.80): only strong hits; quiet calls may be missed.
threshold.example:
Same recording fragment:
threshold 0.40 → 47 labels
threshold 0.55 → 31 labels
threshold 0.70 → 18 labels
Compare on the spectrogram and pick a threshold for your package.
threshold.tip: Start at 0.50. Too many labels—raise by 0.05–0.10. Missed weak calls—lower and verify visually. Save a good threshold in the profile before creating a package.

outputPath.title: Label output path
outputPath.what: Where to save the label file in Audacity/orcAI text format. default means one file per WAV next to the recording, named by orcAI rules (model, channel, _predicted suffix).
outputPath.effect: With default, each file has its own labels—best for packages, spectrograms, and per-file filtering. A single explicit .txt path merges all package WAVs into one file (uncommon; easy to overwrite by mistake).
outputPath.example:
WAV: /project/recordings/site_a/clip_003.wav
Output path: default
→ /project/recordings/site_a/clip_003_c1_orcai-isl-v1_predicted.txt

Output path: /tmp/all_labels.txt
→ all package files write into one file
outputPath.tip: Keep default for field projects. Use an explicit path only when you deliberately want one combined file.

overwrite.title: Overwrite existing result
overwrite.what: Allows orcAI to replace a label file that already exists at the output path. If unchecked, a matching path causes the job to fail and the old file remains.
overwrite.effect: On: every predict run may replace an existing label file. Off: first run is protected; on the Analysis tab, re-analyzing files with existing results still overwrites after confirmation.
overwrite.example:
clip_003_c1_orcai-isl-v1_predicted.txt already exists:
overwrite off → error, file unchanged
overwrite on → new result replaces the old file
overwrite.tip: Before threshold experiments, back up the recordings folder or leave overwrite off so you do not lose a good run.

saveProbabilities.title: Save probabilities
saveProbabilities.what: Besides intervals in the .txt file, orcAI saves detailed probabilities over time (extra data files). The text labels are built the same way; probabilities are for deeper analysis.
saveProbabilities.effect: Uses more disk space and may run slightly longer. Without this option you only get the .txt file—enough for spectrogram review and filtering.
saveProbabilities.example:
clip_003.wav, threshold 0.50:
without probabilities → one *_predicted.txt
with probabilities → *_predicted.txt + probability curve files (names depend on orcAI version)
saveProbabilities.tip: Enable when tuning threshold from curves or exporting to R/Python. For the usual recognize → review → filter cycle, .txt alone is enough.

callDurationLimits.title: Duration limits (during predict)
callDurationLimits.what: Path to a JSON file: per signal class, minimum and maximum segment duration in seconds. orcAI can drop segments outside those bounds during predictions.
callDurationLimits.effect: Path set: only in-range segments appear in the .txt. Empty: all detections are kept; trim by length later on Filtering (handy to compare before/after).
callDurationLimits.tip: Leave empty when first exploring your data. The project JSON path is often filled automatically when the queue loads.

labelSuffix.title: Label suffix
labelSuffix.what: A short marker orcAI uses when writing class names in the label file. Default is asterisk (*). The same value is passed to the filtering step.
labelSuffix.effect: Changing the suffix in the profile after predictions can make Filtering fail to parse existing files. Analysis packages freeze parameters—including suffix—at package creation.
labelSuffix.example:
In the .txt a class may look like: call_a*
Suffix: *

If you set suffix to call, name format changes—older * annotations will not match.
labelSuffix.tip: Do not change * unless required. Change only when reference labels or the model explicitly use another format.

baseDirRecording.title: Recordings folder (CSV)
baseDirRecording.what: Root folder on disk. orcAI prepends it to relative paths in recording_table.csv to locate WAV files for table-driven batch predictions.
baseDirRecording.effect: Used when the queue row is a CSV table entry, not a single project WAV from File selection. Ordinary WAV workflow does not need this field.
baseDirRecording.example:
baseDirRecording: /Users/me/project/recordings
In CSV: site_a/clip_001.wav
orcAI opens: /Users/me/project/recordings/site_a/clip_001.wav
baseDirRecording.tip: Set to the project recordings folder when the table lists relative paths. For typical WAV-only work, leave as is.

verbosity.title: Log verbosity
verbosity.what: How much orcAI writes to the job log (Lab → Jobs), from 0 (errors only) to 3 (verbose debug). Does not change label quality.
verbosity.effect: 0–1: short logs on long packages. 2: normal daily use. 3: maximum detail when debugging failures.
verbosity.example:
0 → ERROR: WAV not found
2 → INFO: processing clip_003.wav …
3 → DEBUG: spectrogram params, tensor shapes …
verbosity.tip: Leave at 2. Use 3 when sending logs to support; for routine packages, 3 adds noise.

annotations.maskNote: Empty class cell = class masked in the annotation, not “no calls”.

pipeline.snippetsShortageBody: The {{split}} table has {{actual}} snippets, but parameters request {{required}} (n_batch_{{split}} × batch_size = {{nBatch}} × {{batch}}). Plain orcAI would fail create-tvt-snippet-tables / train with «larger than available snippets».
pipeline.snippetsShortageDesktop: orcAI Desktop clamps n_batch_* to inventory when at least one full batch remains; otherwise create-tvt / train match CLI and fail. To turn the lamp green, lower n_batch_{{split}} or batch_size.
pipeline.snippetsShortageDesktopClamp: orcAI Desktop clamps n_batch_{{split}} to inventory (≥ 1 batch) before run, so create-tvt / training can still succeed. To turn the lamp green and match CLI parameters, lower n_batch_{{split}} or batch_size.
pipeline.snippetsShortageDesktopNoClamp: Fewer snippets than one full batch — Desktop cannot clamp n_batch_{{split}} without the same orcAI error. Lower n_batch_{{split}} / batch_size or rebuild snippets.
pipeline.hpsearchOutsidePlanHint: This wizard plan did not include hyperparameter search. Cancel the plan to run this step manually.
